items.followUp: Resolve a force of 80 N acting at 60° to the x-axis into its perpendicular components.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the force and its angle to the x-axis.
rubric.description: Records F = 50 N and θ = 30° to the x-axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the force and angle.

rubric.why: Checks the formula and setup for the horizontal component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct x-component formula or its substitution.
Award 1 mark for the correct x-component with unit.

rubric.why: Checks the formula and setup for the vertical component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct y-component formula or its substitution.
Award 1 mark for the correct y-component with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 50 N, θ = 30° to the x-axis.
Horizontal component: Fx = F cos θ = (50 N) cos 30° = 43.3 N.
Vertical component: Fy = F sin θ = (50 N) sin 30° = 25 N.
The perpendicular components are 43.3 N along the x-axis and 25 N along the y-axis.

items.followUp: Define Young’s modulus and derive its expression in terms of force, original length, cross-sectional area and extension.

rubric.why: Checks the definition and the condition under which Young’s modulus applies.
rubric.description: Defines Young’s modulus as the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain within the elastic limit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct ratio and elastic-limit condition.

rubric.why: Checks the expression for tensile stress.
rubric.description: Writes tensile stress = force / cross-sectional area = F/A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct stress expression.

rubric.why: Checks the expression for tensile strain.
rubric.description: Writes tensile strain = extension / original length = ΔL/L.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct strain expression.

rubric.why: Checks the derived expression for Young’s modulus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final expression.

modelAnswer: Young’s modulus is the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain, provided the material is within its elastic limit.
Tensile stress = force / cross-sectional area = F/A.
Tensile strain = extension / original length = ΔL/L.
Young’s modulus, Y = stress / strain = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) = FL/(AΔL).

items.followUp: Convert 12 years into seconds, taking 1 year as 365 days.

modelAnswer: Time = 15 years × 365 days/year × 24 hours/day × 60 minutes/hour × 60 seconds/minute.
